analyst_output.research_question: How can Bayesian optimization efficiently handle black-box functions where the optimal solution lies on unknown physical constraints?
analyst_output.paper_overview: Many real-world design problems are constrained by unknown physical limits, and the best designs often sit on the boundary between feasible and infeasible regions. Standard Bayesian optimization struggles when crossing a constraint causes failure and the feasible set is not known in advance. This paper introduces boundary-focused constrained BO to model that frontier and search near it safely. The method uses neural ensembles to estimate constraint boundaries more flexibly than typical GP classifiers. The goal is higher-performing feasible designs under limited evaluation budgets. Results cover synthetic boundary tasks and real mechanical design benchmarks.
analyst_output.methodology: Propose BE-CBO, a new BO method that learns constraints using an ensemble of neural networks to explore the boundary between feasible and infeasible designs.
variables: Constant factor C for neuron scaling
evaluation_metrics: Number of function evaluations to reach optimum

reported_results.value: One hidden layer insufficient due to underfitting; two or more layers perform similarly
C=64 proved stable, outperforming C=16,32 and matching high-capacity networks

analyst_output.notes: Method is effective when constraints are unknown and optima lie on constraint boundaries. Performance not sensitive to hidden layer count beyond one.
